newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES OF BARCELONA V ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES OF BARCELONA V ATLETICO.

text.p: Facts and figures for Saturday's Spanish first division game between Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

Atletico Madrid: Founded in April 1903 as Athletic de Madrid, a name that was kept until the Spanish Civil War when the club joined forces with Madrid's Club Aviacion. Victorious fascist dictator Francisco Franco forbade the use of anglicised names such as Athletic and Sporting and the club became known as Atletico Aviacion from 1939 until finally changing its name to Atletico de Madrid in 1946. In English this is shortened to Atletico Madrid.

Major honours: League champions: 1940, 1941, 1950, 1951, 1966, 1970, 1973, 1977, 1996. Spanish Cup winners: 1960, 1961, 1965, 1972, 1976, 1985, 1991, 1992, 1996. Cup Winners' Cup 1962. Intercontinental Cup 1975.
Ground: Vicente Calderon stadium (named after a former club president), capacity 56,000.
Trainer: Radomir Antic (Serbia)
Record league appearances: Abelardo, 399 games.
Barcelona: Founded in 1899 by Hans Gamper, a Swiss resident in Barcelona.
Ground: Camp Nou stadium, (meaning the 'new ground' in the Catalan language), capacity 112,000.
Trainer: Bobby Robson (England)
Record league appearances: Migueli, 391.
Barcelona v Atletico Madrid: last five league meetings at Camp Nou (1991-92 first): 1-0, 1-1, 5-3, 4-3, 1-3.
Corresponding match last year: Barcelona 1 (Jordi Cruyff 30) Atletico Madrid 3 (Lyuboslav Penev 15, Juan Vizcaino 53, Leonardo Biagini 85))
Fascinating facts:
-- Barcelona were the first-ever Spanish league champions in 1929 and share with Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid the honour of never having been relegated from the Spanish first division.

-- Atletico have only spent four seasons in the second division but have twice avoided relegation in curious circumstances. In 1934 they were saved by the decision to increase the first division from 10 to 12 teams. Two years later they were again due to go down but the Civil War intervened. When the league restarted in 1939, Oviedo withdrew because their ground had been used as a prison camp. The then Atletico Aviacion stayed in the first division by winning a play-off against Osasuna -- and took the next two league titles!
-- Barcelona boast the largest number of season ticket holders of any club in Europe -- 108,000 -- and averaged gates of 81,000 last season.
-- Barcelona games always begin with the singing of the club hymn, which is written in the local Catalan language.
-- Barcelona are universally known as Barca, with a soft 'c', while Atletico is frequently shortened to 'Atleti'.

-- Atletico are also known as the 'colchoneros' from the Spanish word 'colchon' meaning mattress. Earlier this century mattresses made in Spain were predominantly red and white, the Atletico club colours.
-- Barcelona fans are often known as 'cules', believed to be a corruption of the Spanish word 'coles' meaning cauliflowers, because of the market garden on which Barcelona's former ground was built.
